title: Reconcile tenant metadata stale-index causing operator reconcile loops; staged prune hotpatch
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Several customers running Private/VPC on-prem upgrades observed long-running operator reconcile loops after helm upgrades. Root cause traced to stale tenant metadata indexes (tenant.spec.hashIndex / tenant.status.observedIndex) that diverge when Helm charts perform partial CRD/CR updates during an interrupted upgrade. When the operator sees an index > observedIndex it triggers reconciliation that repeatedly fails because the cached manifest contains legacy annotations; this results in CPU/leader thrash and blocked upgrades for a subset of tenants.

Impact:
- High: multiple on-prem customers reported upgrade timeouts and escalations impacting tenant availability (control-plane reconcile CPU spikes, delayed webhook responses).
- Affected modes: Private (VPC) and air-gapped on-prem installs that used Helm 3.9+ with staged CRD updates.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Use a staging onprem cluster with tenant CRD v1 and operator v2024.11.
2) Simulate interrupted helm upgrade (helm upgrade --atomic killed midway) while CRD/CR manifests include new index annotation on tenant CRs.
3) Observe operator leader log: "observedIndex mismatch" followed by repeated reconcile attempts and patch failures with 409 and schema mismatch errors.

Root cause analysis:
- Inconsistent ordering between Helm's server-side apply and our operator's optimistic index bookkeeping allows tenant.spec.hashIndex to be set before CR status.observedIndex is reconciled by a leader.
- The operator's stale-index detection code currently treats index delta as absolute source-of-truth and attempts full manifest reapply, but does not robustly sanitize legacy annotations or tolerate partial CRD schemas, causing patch rejection and retry storms.

Mitigation implemented so far (short-term):
- Quick server-side hotpatch (deployed to staging and two impacted customers) that adds a pruning pass: when reconcile detects delta > threshold and patch returns 409/schema error, operator performs a targeted prune of legacy annotations and retries as a single transactional apply.
- Added circuit-breaker: if reconcile retries exceed 6 attempts in 5m, operator marks tenant as "upgrade-quarantine" and reduces reconcile frequency to avoid control-plane storming while alerting ops.

Planned work (this ticket):
1) Harden reconcile algorithm: introduce idempotent preflight sanitizer that drops historical helm-managed annotations and normalizes known legacy fields before any patch attempt.
2) Implement deterministic index handshake: leader will write a provisional observedIndex marker to status and wait for propagation before treating upstream hashIndex as authoritative.
3) Expand prune hotpatch to a staged release: canary to affected customers, then Broad. Provide rollback knob (env VAR OP_PRUNE_STRICT=false).
4) Add telemetry: counts of stale-index reconciles, prune successes/failures, quarantine activations per tenant.
5) Run chaos tests: simulate interrupted upgrades and ensure operator converges within SLO.

Acceptance criteria:
- No customer escalations with stale-index-induced reconcile storms in canary group for 72h.
- Operator converges tenant state without >5 reconcile retries for interrupted helm upgrades in integration tests.
- Metrics emitted and documented in runbook.

Rollback plan:
- Toggle OP_PRUNE_STRICT=false to disable prune hotpatch immediately.
- If operator continues to destabilize, fallback plan is to roll operator to previous stable image and coordinate manual tenant metadata repair script run for affected tenants (script checked into repo).
